extracted.intended_audience: state air agencies and other state officials preparing CAA section 111(d) state plan submissions for affected electric generating units (EGUs); state plan developers and regulators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements for preparing and submitting state plans under EPA emission guidelines for CO2 from affected EGUs, including required plan components, documentation, demonstration of equivalent emission reductions, and public engagement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence to presumptive unit-specific rate-based standards
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must demonstrate that they achieve the level of emission reduction that would result if each affected source was individually achieving its presumptive standard of performance, after accounting for any application of RULOF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States have discretion to establish standards and compliance flexibilities, but plans must achieve an equivalent level of emission reduction as applying EPA's presumptive standards. Plans must document and support processes and underlying data used to establish standards, and provide methods, assumptions, and calculations necessary for EPA to determine equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cannot rely on reductions at non-affected sources
rubrics_metrics.description: States cannot rely on or account for emission reductions occurring at non-affected sources to demonstrate compliance with these emission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only emission reductions at affected EGUs may count towards compliance with the state plan, including for demonstrating equivalence of compliance flexibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit-specific backstop emission limitation for mass-based compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans that include mass-based compliance flexibilities must apply a unit-specific backstop rate for all participating affected EGUs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The backstop rate is necessary to ensure consistency with achieving the emission reductions required under CAA section 111(a)(1). EPA will apply high scrutiny to assumptions about utilization for units participating in mass-based compliance approaches and mass-based trading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass-based trading permissible with constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is allowing states to include mass-based emission trading for affected coal-fired EGUs in the medium- and long-term subcategories, subject to requirements and caveats (including use of a unit-specific backstop rate and demonstration of equivalence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA is not providing a presumptively approvable mass-based trading approach; states must demonstrate equivalence to unit-specific rate-based compliance, show how the mass limit is calculated and justify assumptions (e.g., utilization), and specify allowance distribution and other program design features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mass budget calculation and utilization assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish a mass budget, states must use the rate-based standard of performance and an assumed level of utilization for each participating affected EGU, summing individual mass limits to an aggregate mass budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must specify how allowances are distributed and the basis for utilization assumptions. EPA warns that projecting utilization is increasingly challenging and will scrutinize assumptions, because an improper assumption for one EGU can affect others in the trading program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance mechanics: issuance, surrender, and tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: A mass-based trading program must define allowances (each representing 1 ton CO2), issuance amounts, surrender requirements based on reported emissions, and include a tracking system for tradable compliance instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must establish mechanics for demonstrating compliance (e.g., surrender of compliance instruments based on monitoring and reporting), continuous monitoring and reporting of CO2 emissions and generation, and tracking system development. EPA can provide technical support and states may consider using EPA's allowance management system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstration of compliance with unit-specific backstop rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Each participating affected EGU in a mass-based program must demonstrate compliance with the unit-specific backstop rate in addition to participating in mass-based trading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The backstop mitigates concerns about program calibration; states must include implementation and enforcement provisions that ensure units meet the backstop requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: High degree of scrutiny for utilization assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA will apply a high degree of scrutiny to assumptions about the utilization of affected EGUs participating in mass-based trading or mass-based compliance approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because utilization projections are uncertain (due to technology, fuel prices, electricity demand), assumptions must be conservative and well-documented; EPA may reject plans that do not convincingly support equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification and justification of other trading program design features
rubrics_metrics.description: States must specify the structure and purpose of any other trading program design feature(s) (e.g., mass budget adjustment mechanism) and explain how they impact the demonstration of an equivalent level of emission reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design features must be shown not to undermine equivalence; documentation should explain impacts on program stringency and calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: General emission averaging/trading program implementation systems
rubrics_metrics.description: States must establish procedures and systems necessary to implement and enforce an emission averaging or trading program, including mechanics for compliance demonstration, continuous monitoring and reporting, and a tracking system for instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes setting up monitoring and reporting requirements, instrument surrender mechanics, and systems to enforce compliance. EPA technical assistance may be available and states may leverage existing EPA or non-EPA trading infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling differing compliance dates in trading/averaging programs
rubrics_metrics.description: States must consider differing compliance dates for affected EGUs when designing averaging or trading programs and may initially include only sources with a common compliance date (e.g., Jan 1, 2030) and add others later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding sources as their standards begin to apply is the most straightforward approach and was supported by commenters; plans must account for how new additions factor into aggregate standards or mass budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance banking considerations and safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: States must consider whether to allow allowance banking and recognize that unrestricted banking may produce long-term allowance surpluses that undermine program stringency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA suggests restricting banking or implementing recalibration mechanisms (e.g., annual bank recalibration) to prevent surplus accumulation; the unit-specific backstop can mitigate but not eliminate these risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interstate trading consistency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Interstate emission trading programs are permissible but require that all participating states use the same form of trading, have consistent design elements and identical trading program requirements, and each submit an individual state plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each state must include provisions ensuring affected EGUs in their state are in compliance considering actions of EGUs in other states. EPA requests all related state plan submissions before evaluating any of them to ensure consistency and may provide technical assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on presumptively approvable mass-based trading
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA is not providing a presumptively approvable mass-based trading approach because of heightened risk in calculating a correct mass budget and reduced universe of covered sources under the final guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States may still develop their own mass-based trading approaches but must meet equivalence demonstrations and backstop requirements; EPA will scrutinize utilization assumptions and program design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative completeness criteria for plan submission
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete state plan submission must include: (1) formal submittal letter from Governor or designee; (2) evidence of adoption in state code or issuance of final document with dates; (3) evidence of legal authority; (4) copy of regulation/document (signed/stamped/dated) with changes noted; (5) evidence state followed procedural requirements; (6) evidence public notice given consistent with 40 CFR 60.23a; (7) certification public hearings held as required; (8) compilation of public comments and state's responses; (9) documentation of meaningful engagement (stakeholders list, summary of engagement/input, description of consideration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic copies must be exact duplicates of hard copies where possible; include cover page and table of contents if copying existing publications. Documentation of meaningful engagement is required as an administrative completeness element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical completeness criteria for plan submission
rubrics_metrics.description: All plans must meet technical criteria including: (1) description of plan approach and geographic scope; (2) identification of each designated facility, standards of performance for each affected EGU, and monitoring/recordkeeping/reporting to determine compliance; (3) identification of compliance schedules and/or increments of progress; (4) demonstration that the plan will achieve emission performance under applicable guidelines; (5) documentation of state recordkeeping and reporting to determine plan performance; (6) demonstration that each standard is quantifiable, permanent, verifiable, enforceable, and non-duplicative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These criteria come from 40 CFR part 60, subpart Ba; plans must provide documentation and data sufficient for EPA to assess projection and enforceability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of performance characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of performance for affected EGUs must be quantifiable, verifiable, permanent, enforceable, non-duplicative, and continuous in nature (per CAA section 302(l)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must express standards in the specified units (see related criterion) and ensure regulatory provisions for implementation and enforcement are included in the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required identification of affected EGUs and subcategory assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must identify each affected EGU and the subcategory to which each affected EGU is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must include identification of standards of performance for each affected EGU and associated monitoring, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of coal-fired EGUs committing to permanent cessation before 2032
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans must include, in the regulatory portion, a list of existing coal-fired steam-generating EGUs that plan to permanently cease operation before January 1, 2032, and the calendar dates by which they committed to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The plan must provide that an EGU operating past the listed date is no longer exempt and is in violation, except where a time-limited extension under the reliability assurance mechanism applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Units for expressing standards of performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards of performance must be expressed in lb CO2/MWh gross basis, or for low-load natural gas- and oil-fired subcategories, lb CO2/MMBtu; or if state allows mass-based compliance, tons CO2 per year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When states provide compliance flexibilities, they must also identify the presumptive unit-specific rate-based standard that would apply absent the flexibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline emission performance data requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For each affected EGU, state plans must identify baseline emission performance including CO2 mass and electricity generation data (or heat input data for low-load subcategories) from 40 CFR part 75 reporting for the 5-year period immediately prior to publication of the final rule, and identify which continuous 8-quarter period from that 5-year period was used to calculate baseline performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States must include the data and documentation sufficient for EPA to understand and replicate calculations for establishing unit-specific baselines and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when using compliance flexibilities (identification and demonstration)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a state uses a compliance flexibility (e.g., mass limit, aggregate emission rate limitation, averaging/trading), the plan must identify the presumptive unit-specific rate-based standard (lb CO2/MWh-gross) that would apply absent the flexibility; the actual standard applied under the flexibility and how it is calculated; implementation and enforcement provisions for the flexibility; identification of the unit-specific backstop for mass-based flexibilities; and a demonstration that the plan will achieve an equivalent level of emission reduction as individual rate-based standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must provide methods, assumptions, and calculations necessary for EPA to review the flexibility and determine equivalence; documentation must show how the flexibility ensures equivalent (or better) emission reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increments of progress, reporting obligations, and enforceable milestones
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include increments of progress and reporting obligations and milestones as enforceable elements for affected EGUs within applicable subcategories or pursuant to consideration of RULOF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These elements are enforceable portions of the plan and must be clearly specified in the regulatory provisions of the plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceable commitment to permanently cease operation for certain units
rubrics_metrics.description: For affected EGUs in the medium-term coal-fired subcategory and EGUs relying on a plan to permanently cease operation for a less stringent standard pursuant to RULOF, the state plan must include an enforceable commitment to permanently cease operation by a date certain and identify the calendar dates of commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commitment must be enforceable and plans must clearly identify the dates; operation past the date means the unit is no longer exempt and is in violation except where an approved time-limited extension applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement that existing coal-fired EGUs operate only under the plan's standard or an exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must provide that any existing coal-fired steam-generating EGU shall operate only subject to a standard of performance pursuant to these emission guidelines or under an exemption from applicability provided under 40 CFR 60.5850b.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes any time-limited extension of a date for ceasing operation pursuant to the reliability assurance mechanism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: State plans must include monitoring, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements for affected EGUs sufficient to determine compliance and performance of the plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes CO2 emissions and generation monitoring (or heat input for specified subcategories) consistent with 40 CFR part 75 reporting, continuous monitoring systems where applicable, and documentation to allow EPA replication of calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation to enable EPA review and replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans must adequately document and support the process, methods, and underlying data used to establish standards of performance and compliance flexibilities so EPA can understand and replicate calculations and determine if the plan achieves equivalent emission reductions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include data and documentation (CO2 mass, generation or heat input, assumptions, methods, calculations) from the 5-year part 75 period and specify the 8-quarter baseline selection; provide transparent methods for enforcement and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful engagement requirement and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: States must conduct meaningful engagement: defined as 'timely engagement with pertinent stakeholders and/or their representatives in the plan development or plan revision process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engagement should not be disproportionate in favor of certain stakeholders, should be informed by best practices, and pertinent stakeholders include, but are not limited to, industry, small businesses, and communities most affected by and/or vulnerable to plan impacts. Plans must document meaningful engagement (list of stakeholders, summary of engagement and input received, description of how input was considered).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of pertinent stakeholders and tailored engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: States should use the EPA discussion of potential impacts to help identify pertinent stakeholders and tailor meaningful engagement to state- and source-specific circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA recognizes state diversity and does not finalize additional requirements on stakeholder identification; states should consider communities most affected or vulnerable, energy communities, and energy workers, and apply best practices from the preamble to subpart Ba.
